origins.section: A Virtual Thread That Waits Gives Its Carrier Back, So a Few Platform Threads Run Thousands of Requests
A Virtual Thread That Computes Keeps Its Carrier: Java 21 Has No Time Slice
A Waiting Virtual Thread Keeps Its Stack, and Everything It References, on the Heap
One Thread per Task Means Nothing Per-Thread Is Reused: Pool the Expensive Object, Not the Thread

recorded.outcome:q-burst-of-database-waits: Lines 43-46: one carrier per processor; at a blocking JDK call (socket read) the frames go to the heap and the carrier picks up the next ready virtual thread. Lines 34-39: 10,000 one-second waits on one carrier took 1,054 ms.
